display.title: Episode 273: The Flickering Flame (Rosh Chodesh Iyar)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show without music: why Rosh Chodesh is the 'head' of the month, respect for others, the precious gift of time, and a shoemaker's lamp that teaches about teshuvah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5747, during Sefirah, so the program opens without music. Uncle Yossi explains why the first day of the month is called Rosh Chodesh, the head: every day of the month draws its strength from it, so we should improve our davening, brachos, tzedakah and respect for others. He tells why we do not listen to music during Sefirah: Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague because they did not show respect to one another, so these weeks are a time to practice honor for parents, teachers and friends, and to bring peace and unity, our answer to 'Ad Mosai'. Counting the Omer shows that every day counts; the story of little Miriam who cried over a lost dime teaches not to waste time. A boy of almost five recites the Shema. Story time: on a snowy night the tzaddik Rabbi Yisrael shelters with an old shoemaker who worked late because his lamp still had oil, saying 'as long as the candle burns, one can still repair'. Rabbi Yisrael draws the lesson: while we live we can always do teshuvah. The show ends with the Lag BaOmer parade announcement.
display.lesson: As long as the candle is burning, one can still repair: use every day of life to learn, do mitzvos and do teshuvah.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: 'welcoming the new month of Iyar... tonight we say Yaaleh V'yavo'; Lag BaOmer is Sunday, May 17.

advisories.note: Explains that thousands of Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague.

privacy.note: The Shema guest is named in full, with his age and school.

sources_cited.note: 'Love peace and pursue peace' (Ohev shalom v'rodef shalom).
'So that your days be lengthened', from the second paragraph of the Shema.
Rabbi Akiva's students did not show respect to one another.
